subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- October 28, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - October 28, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS community,

We're excited to share the latest updates from our community and development team. First, we'd like to highlight the recent blog post by Peter Robinson on Fedora support for Raspberry Pi 5. This insightful article provides a comprehensive overview of the current state of Fedora's support for the latest Raspberry Pi model. If you're interested in learning more about this topic, be sure to check it out.

In other news, we've received security updates from AlmaLinux, which include patches for bind, bind9.18, brotli, buildah, container-tools, firefox, flatpak, freeipmi, gcc, golang, grafana, httpd, and more. These updates are now available for AcreetionOS users, ensuring the continued security and stability of our distribution.

On the development front, our team has been actively working on various projects. We've made several commits to our codebase, including updates to AcreetionOS-Xlibre, acreetionos-immutable, and acreetionos-code-acreetionos. These changes aim to improve the overall performance and user experience of our distribution.

One notable commit is the update to our release process, which now includes a fix for the release.yml block-scalar indentation issue that was causing workflow validation problems. Additionally, we've re-triggered the GitLab mirror and made explicit shellcheck on top-level scripts in acreetionos-code-acreetionos.

We're also proud to highlight the contributions of our community members. Our team has been actively engaging with the community, providing support and guidance on various topics. If you have any questions or need help with AcreetionOS, please don't hesitate to reach out to our Discord server or GitHub repository.

As we continue to work on improving our distribution, we're committed to transparency and open communication. We encourage you to stay up-to-date with our latest developments by following our blog, GitHub repository, and social media channels.

In other news, our team has been exploring ways to improve the user experience of AcreetionOS. We're working on various features and enhancements that will make our distribution even more user-friendly and efficient.

We'd like to thank our community for their continued support and enthusiasm. Your contributions and feedback are invaluable to us, and we're grateful for the opportunity to work together to create a better Linux distribution.

As always, we're committed to providing a secure, private, and user-friendly Linux experience. If you have any questions or suggestions, please don't hesitate to reach out to us. We're always here to help.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva and Darren Clift
Co-Lead Developers, AcreetionOS
